messages.subject: Re: Customizing activityOverlap plots
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jennie,
you are right, currently the three text items in the plot you mentioned cannot be changed.
But because the function activityOverlap is basically nothing but a convenient wrapper around the function overlapPlot from the overlap package you can also use that function instead. All you need to do is convert the time of day to radial time (which ranges from 0 to 2 pi). Then, you can use the overlapPlot function to your heart's desire. Here's a little convenience function which converts a time vector to radial time (omitting the date information). Adjust timeformat to match your data (it should work with the default output of recordTable).

ClocktimeToTimeRad <- function(Clocktime,
                               timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"){

  DateTime2 <- strptime(as.character(Clocktime), format = timeformat, tz = "UTC")
  Time2     <- format(DateTime2, format = "%H:%M:%S", usetz = FALSE)
  Time.rad  <- (as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime(Time2, format = "%H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))) -
                  as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime("0", format = "%S", tz = "UTC")))) / 3600 * (pi/12)
  return(Time.rad)
}

Here's an example for running it with the sample data:

data("recordTableSample")
recordTableSample$TimeRad <- ClocktimeToTimeRad(recordTableSample$DateTimeOriginal)

and for generating the plot:

# choose species
speciesA <- "VTA"
speciesB <- "PBE"

# set legend parameters. You can play around with these
legendPosition <- "topleft"
legendText <- c(speciesA, speciesB)
lty.tmp <- c(1, 2)
lwd.tmp <- c(1, 1)
col.tmp <- c("black", "blue")

# do plot
overlapPlot(A = recordTableSample[recordTableSample$Species == speciesA, "TimeRad"],
            B = recordTableSample[recordTableSample$Species == speciesB, "TimeRad"],
            main = "")

# add legend
legend(x = legendPosition,
       legend = legendText,
       lty = lty.tmp,
       lwd = lwd.tmp,
       col = col.tmp,
       bg = "white"
)

Which gives me this:

messages.subject: Re: Importing data from existing Excel sheets
messages.subject_clean: Importing data from existing Excel sheets
messages.body_plain:
Hi Roberto,
the table you attached is very similar to what the function recordTable will give as output, and you can make it usable in camtrapR easily. The bare minimum you need in that record table is a station column (you have that), a species column (you got that too), and a Date/time column (which you can create easily from the two separate columns you have). This will give the essential information about which species was seen where and when.

Here's the steps you need to do:

1. load table into R, preferably from a csv file to avoid Excel causing a mess (could easily happen in your Time column with Excel interpreting as dates).

2. make a date/time column. Assuming you load this table as a data.frame called records, you can create that column with something like:
records$DateTimeOriginal <- strptime(paste(records$Date, records$Time, sep = " "), format = "%d-%b-%y %H:%M")     # i didn't test this. If it doesn't work check ?strptime

3. Create an equivalent to the camera trap station table that is returned by data(camtraps)   (note the Problem columns are not necessary, and station column values in this table must match values of station column in your record table. This is also detailed in the package vignette)

That should be it. By not extracting data from your images, you will not be able to get additional metadata information that are stored in the images, be it technical information or some tags you assigned to the images. But you probably don't necessarily need them and you'll be able to use most functions in the package this way.

messages.subject: Re: Graph for Activity overlap
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sally,
currently this is not supported in the package. What you could do for visualisation is use the output of the function activityDensity from camtrapR (which is radial time, or alternatively the function ClocktimeToTimeRad which you find in my respones to the question Customozing activityOverlap plots her in the group) and put that into the densityPlot function from the overlap package for single species. Output will be x and y coordinates of the activity kernel density estimation. These you could then combine into a common plot.

Here's the rough idea:

library(overlap)

list_records_radial_time <- activityDensity(recordTable = recordTableSample,
                allSpecies  = TRUE,
                writePNG    = FALSE,
                plotR       = F)

str(list_records_radial_time)
names(list_records_radial_time)
densities <- lapply(list_records_radial_time, densityPlot)

plot(densities[[1]], type = "l", ylim = c(0, max(sapply(densities, FUN = function(df){df$y}))))   # plot densities of first species in list
lines(densities[[2]], col = "red")
lines(densities[[3]], col = "blue")

Currently, this feature is not implemented. But I agree it would be a good idea to include it in the future. I'll put in on the list of features to add.
In the meantime you can use the function ClocktimeToTimeRad below to calculate radial time from the clock time of your records which is needed for the functions in the overlap package.
Thank you for the suggestion!
Jürgen

## function to convert clock time (formatted as "2016-12-31 23:59:59") to Radial time (omitting the date information).

ClocktimeToTimeRad <- function(Clocktime,
                               timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"){

  DateTime2 <- strptime(as.character(Clocktime), format = timeformat, tz = "UTC")
  Time2     <- format(DateTime2, format = "%H:%M:%S", usetz = FALSE)
  Time.rad  <- (as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime(Time2, format = "%H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC"))) -
                  as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime("0", format = "%S", tz = "UTC")))) / 3600 * (pi/12)
  return(Time.rad)
}

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jürgen, hi all
I finally decided to move all files to the Species Folder (from the "number-of-individuals-per-species" folder). Now everything seems to work well (recorTable,....). Here's the script I have used to move all files, in case some of you needs it someday:

wd<-("YOUR_FOLDER_OF PICTURES")
dirStat<-list.files(wd, full.names = TRUE)
for (i in 1:length(dirStat)){                                            #in each Station
  dirCamInStat<-list.files(dirStat[i], full.names = TRUE)
  for (j in 1:length(dirCamInStat)){                                 #in each Camera
    dirSpsInCam<-list.files(dirCamInStat[j], full.names = TRUE)
    for (k in 1:length(dirSpsInCam)){                               #in each Species
      dirNumIndPerSpecies<-list.files(dirSpsInCam[k], full.names = TRUE)
      for (y in 1:length(dirNumIndPerSpecies)){                #in each NumberPerSpecies
        origFolder<-list.files(dirNumIndPerSpecies[y], full.names=TRUE, recursive=TRUE)
        destFolder<-dirSpsInCam[k]
        file.copy(origFolder, destFolder, copy.date = TRUE)
        unlink(dirNumIndPerSpecies[y], recursive = TRUE)     #delete the NumberOfSpecies folder
      }#endNumberPerSpecies
    }#end Species
  }#end Camera
} #end Station

Best
Bernat
